selection_policy: Exact category expansion is deterministic. Rules classify and explain candidates but never silently remove a candidate from a selected category.

rules.rule: A permit is required to construct, enlarge, alter, repair, move, demolish, or change occupancy of a building or structure, and to install, alter, repair, remove, convert, or replace regulated electrical, gas, mechanical, plumbing, or elevator systems.
Submit scaled drawings for all work. New residences, additions, pools, and accessory structures require sealed plot plans; interior work with no footprint change does not require a plot plan.

The non-DRC route is limited to interior commercial repair, remodel, or tenant finish with no footprint enlargement or occupancy change. New buildings, additions, and occupancy changes route through Development Review; floodplain parcels use the floodplain DRC form.
Review uses the locally adopted 2018 IBC, IRC, IMC, UPC, IEBC, IECC and IFC; the 2017 NEC; current NFPA Life Safety standards; and Unified Government amendments.
Submit at least two construction-document sets where required. A Kansas registered design professional must prepare documents unless a code exception or building-official waiver applies.
An application may be treated as abandoned after 180 days. A permit expires if work does not begin within 180 days or is suspended or abandoned for 180 days.
Starting regulated work before the permit is issued can double the permit fee and does not authorize noncompliant work.
Building Inspection applications are submitted to buildinginspection@wycokck.org; email attachments must not exceed 25 MB.
The published fee schedule adds $5 when a trade permit is obtained by phone or fax.
Schedule inspections at 913-573-8620 at least 24 hours ahead and provide the permit number. Approved stamped plans, posted address, permit, and inspection card must be onsite.

Applicable inspections include footing, foundation wall, underslab plumbing, sewer, water service/BPU, all-trades rough-in, framing, electrical, plumbing, HVAC, rated assemblies, lath/gypsum, fireplace, and final. Occupancy is prohibited before final approval.
Published repeat reinspection fees escalate from $100 to $150, $225, and $337.50.

Before demolition, obtain electric and water disconnect evidence from BPU, gas termination evidence, and sewer abandonment approval or no-service memos. Hauling requires a hauling permit; a street/ROW dumpster requires an Engineering permit.
Demolition requires an open basement/foundation inspection and a final inspection, requested at least 24 hours in advance.

A building permit is required to erect, alter, rebuild, or reface a sign. Plans must show dimensions, materials, construction, site, and illumination; owner consent is required. Repainting or reposting an outdoor sign surface is exempt.
No building or demolition permit affecting a local historic landmark or district may issue before the required Certificate of Appropriateness or historic review.

A complete planning submittal includes the application and fee, owner authorization, legal description in editable Word format, photos, and the dimensioned plans and studies marked for the application type. Kansas professional engineers must seal engineering documents.
The listed hearing applications require a neighborhood meeting, notice at least 14 days beforehand, and posted site signage at least 21 days before the hearing.

Projects involving external physical changes to land or structures other than ordinary single-family work route through Development Review. Commercial building permits follow acceptance of streets/utilities and final-plan approval when required.
Obtain a floodplain certificate before grading, fill, or construction in the regulatory floodplain and use the floodplain DRC building application when applicable.

A land-use permit is required for nonagricultural use of open or vacant land, including stand-alone parking, vehicle storage/salvage, storage yards, ranges, commercial recreation, dumps/landfills, picnic/fishing uses, cemeteries, and nurseries.

Work that disrupts or occupies public right-of-way requires a work-, location-, and date-specific permit. Keep it onsite. Emergency work must be reported by the next business day; extensions or changed scope need supplemental approval; unpermitted work can incur double fees.

An oversize or overweight construction load requires Public Works route approval for the specific vehicle/load dimensions, route, and dates, with insurance documentation as required by the application.

An approved erosion-control plan is required before land-disturbance issuance. Disturbance of one acre or more is specifically covered by the published application and may trigger additional stormwater requirements.

Blasting requires the relevant Fire Prevention storage approval and Engineer use approval, Kansas blaster/user licenses, UG business licenses, preblast survey, at least $5 million insurance, and a $100,000 bond.

Utility work is split among Building Inspection, BPU, Water Pollution Control, and Public Works. The private building permit does not replace the separate service, tap, abandonment, inspection, or right-of-way approval.
Submit system plans, specifications/calculations, and licensed-contractor information to Fire Prevention. Fire sprinkler applications require two plan sets and Fire Prevention approval.
Where hazardous-material quantities or operations trigger the fire code, obtain Fire Chief/Fire Prevention approval before the building permit may issue.

Commercial land-clearing burning and other nonrecreational burning require Fire Department authorization and must follow the published seasonal and equipment limitations, including air-curtain destructor requirements when applicable.

Obtain Kansas construction-stormwater authorization before disturbing one acre or more, including a smaller site that is part of a common plan of development disturbing one acre or more; calculate the entire common-plan disturbance rather than only the current phase.

Prepare and implement a site-specific SWP2 and erosion/sediment controls before disturbance; reconcile disturbed area, drainage, receiving waters, controls, inspection schedule, stabilization, and operator information across the NOI, SWP2, and civil plans.

Keep KDHE authorization, inspections, corrective actions, and stabilization records active through final stabilization and submit the required termination record before treating stormwater coverage as closed.

For demolition of a regulated facility, complete an asbestos inspection and submit the Kansas demolition notification at least ten working days before demolition even when no regulated asbestos is found; verify facility type and number of dwelling units.

Facility identity, owner/operator, asbestos survey, demolition contractor, start/end dates, waste destination, and demolition method must agree across the KDHE notice, UG demolition permit, and project documents.

Use the facility asbestos inspection to identify, classify, quantify, and locate regulated asbestos-containing material and determine the applicable Kansas/NESHAP notification and abatement requirements; unsupported assumptions are not a pass.

Submit the required asbestos renovation/abatement notification at least ten working days before regulated work unless an authorized exception applies, and verify revisions when dates, quantities, methods, or contractors change.

Verify current Kansas asbestos contractor, supervisor, worker, inspector, and project-designer credentials applicable to the work, together with containment, air monitoring, disposal, and closeout records.

Require Kansas food-establishment plan review for new construction, conversion, or qualifying remodel of a food establishment before construction and licensing; classify the operation from the actual menu, processes, service model, and risk rather than the business name.

Reconcile the menu, scaled floor plan, equipment schedule and listings, plumbing, ventilation, warewashing, handwashing, food protection, finishes, storage, refuse, water, sewer, and employee facilities across the food plan and building/trade documents.

Do not begin regulated food operation until plan-review comments are resolved, construction matches the accepted food plan, the preopening inspection is approved, and the required Kansas food license is issued.

Public and semipublic pool construction or alteration requires Health Department plan approval; verify pool geometry, bather load, circulation, turnover, filtration, disinfection, water quality, drains, barriers, decks, accessibility, safety equipment, and support spaces against the controlling pool code.

Pool dimensions, volumes, flow rates, pipe sizes, equipment, electrical bonding, barriers, drainage, and accessibility must agree across health, architectural, structural, plumbing, electrical, and site plans.
Resolve plan-review comments and obtain required construction inspections and health acceptance before filling or operating the public or semipublic pool.

A public or semipublic pool requires a current operator permit separate from construction plan approval; verify the approved pool identity, responsible operator, inspection status, water-quality records, safety equipment, and operating conditions.
Keep the operator permit, required inspections, testing logs, corrective actions, closures, and renewal current throughout operation; construction approval alone is not authorization to operate.

Classify the operation for categorical industrial user, significant industrial user, prohibited-discharge, local-limit, and high-strength-waste requirements using actual processes, chemicals, flows, and pollutant data.

The wastewater application must identify processes, production, flows, pollutants, sampling points, pretreatment, spill controls, slug-discharge potential, monitoring, and certification; reconcile these facts with plumbing and process plans.

Obtain the issued discharge permit before regulated discharge and comply with effluent limits, monitoring, reporting, recordkeeping, notification, pretreatment operation, and changed-discharge approval conditions.

Use official route and right-of-way records to determine whether proposed permanent or construction access affects the Kansas state highway system; a local address or UG permit does not exclude KDOT jurisdiction.

Verify access location, spacing, sight distance, traffic generation, turn lanes, drainage, geometry, traffic control, utilities, restoration, and construction details against KDOT requirements and the issued permit conditions.
Obtain KDOT approval before constructing, altering, or using regulated highway access and complete required inspections, bonds, restoration, and acceptance before closeout.

Determine from official highway right-of-way and utility plans whether any utility occupies, crosses, attaches within, or performs work in KDOT right-of-way; local utility and UG approvals do not replace KDOT authorization.

Verify utility alignment, profile, depth, casing, clearances, structures, crossings, work method, traffic control, erosion control, restoration, and conflicts against the KUPS application and KDOT conditions.
Obtain the KDOT utility permit before right-of-way work and complete required notifications, inspection, as-built information, restoration, and acceptance before closing the authorization.

Calculate uncontrolled and controlled potential to emit for every new or modified stationary emission unit and pollutant, including fugitive emissions where applicable, to determine Kansas construction-permit, approval, registration, and federal-program applicability.

Reconcile process rates, fuels and materials, emission factors, controls, stacks, operating schedules, modeling, monitoring, and requested limits across the air application, equipment specifications, mechanical plans, and operations narrative.

Obtain required KDHE air construction approval before beginning construction or modification and comply with testing, monitoring, recordkeeping, operating, and startup conditions before treating the source as approved.

Use an aquatic-resource delineation and, when obtained, an approved jurisdictional determination to identify waters and wetlands; absence from a generalized map is not evidence that Section 404 does not apply.

Quantify permanent and temporary discharge of dredged or fill material by aquatic resource, verify avoidance and minimization, select the correct nationwide or individual permit path, and provide mitigation when required.
Obtain required Corps verification or permit before discharge and comply with general, regional, species, historic, water-quality, mitigation, construction, reporting, and closeout conditions.

Determine from official USACE project records whether work alters, occupies, or could impair a federally authorized levee or other civil works project; Section 408 applicability is independent of Section 404.

Provide plans, engineering and risk analysis, geotechnical and hydraulic information, environmental and cultural-resource documentation, real-estate rights, construction controls, and operation/maintenance effects required for the Section 408 review.
Obtain written Section 408 permission before affecting the federal project and comply with construction coordination, inspection, as-built, restoration, and closeout conditions.

Verify the official parcel zoning, overlays and historic status, proposed and existing uses, approved plans, special uses, variances, nonconforming rights, and every applicable district or supplemental-use condition from authoritative records.

Calculate and compare lot configuration, density, height, setbacks, parking, loading, landscaping, screening, signs, access, utilities, drainage, public improvements, and design standards against the controlling district, approved plan, and application criteria.

Legal description, ownership, boundaries, uses, dimensions, access, easements, utilities, drainage, architecture, landscaping, signs, phasing, deviations, and conditions must agree across applications, surveys, plats, plans, studies, ordinances, and dependent permits.

Complete every required neighborhood meeting, notice, posting, staff, Planning Commission, Board, governing-body, recording, and condition-resolution step; an application or recommendation is not an issued approval.

Verify survey control, work limits, existing conditions, utility conflicts, engineering design, materials, traffic and pedestrian control, erosion and drainage, easements, restoration, and responsible professional credentials against the exact Public Works or utility workflow.

Reconcile route, location, dates, quantities, connections, elevations, capacities, closures, access, utility service, restoration, and related approvals across civil plans, utility records, traffic plans, building plans, and the issued permit.

Obtain every required UG, BPU, Water Pollution Control, state, and outside-agency authorization before occupying or disturbing right-of-way, connecting utilities, hauling, blasting, closing streets, or constructing public infrastructure.

Complete required notifications, inspections, testing, compaction or material records, corrections, restoration, as-builts, bonds, maintenance periods, and agency acceptance before closeout or service activation.

Identify occupancy, hazards, water supply and fire flow, required fire-protection systems, adopted standards, design criteria, impairments, and interfaces with the approved building life-safety strategy.

Verify layout, coverage, device selection, hydraulic or electrical calculations, supervision, sequence of operations, emergency power, controls, monitoring, access, fire department connections, listings, and coordination across fire, civil, architectural, electrical, and mechanical documents.

Verify the permit holder, designer, installer, supervising contractor, and required Kansas or Unified Government credentials for the exact fire-protection, blasting, hazardous-material, or operational scope.

Complete required rough and final inspections, flushing, pressure, alarm, integrated, functional, radio-coverage, and acceptance tests and resolve every deficiency before activation, occupancy, or operation.
